title: Tramline shift curation & temporary runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight personal passdown for the Tramline shift (overnight coverage). Meant to be quick to scan — not a canonical runbook. Use to triage common flaps and apply temporary mitigations until a proper fix lands.

Top-of-shift checklist (5 minutes):
- Check PagerDuty queue for any open incidents (filter: service:tramline*).
- Glance at Grafana: tramline-overall-latency [last 15m], request_error_rate, model-cache-hit-rate.
- Confirm ded pool sizes: curl -s http://infra-api.internal/dedicated/pools | jq '.tramline'
- Confirm scheduled rollouts: look at ENGINF-128 notes (linked above).

Known recurring issues and quick fixes:
1) KV-cache thrash after model warmup (most common)
   - Symptoms: spike in tail latency, many small token generation requests, cache-miss ratio jumps > 30%.
   - Quick mitigation: temporarily increase KV cache TTL on the affected pool:
     - kubectl -n serving patch config tramline-cache --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"kvTTLSeconds":900}}'
     - Note: this is a soft workaround; record in SRE-3421 if you apply.
   - Follow-up: schedule a probe to capture sequence length distribution for a 1-hour window.

2) Fallthrough to hosted-api during Dedicated pool OOMs
   - Symptoms: error rate from dedicated nodes, fallback logs show "fallback=hosted-api-v2".
   - Quick mitigation: scale up ded-flatpool by +1 node and enable temporary routing exception:
     - open infra dashboard -> pools -> ded-flatpool -> increase replicas to current+1 (canary first if < 2 changes in hour).
     - In extreme cases, toggle route precedence: set policy tramline-route to prefer ded-flatpool for customer-tier:standard.
   - After: monitor served_by label in traces for 10m. if fallback persists, escalate to on-call infra (tag: @infra-oncall).

3) Model artifact mismatch after a deploy
   - Symptoms: model version logs don't match catalog (errors like "KV: missing tokenizer"), sudden rise in output errors or bad generations.
   - Quick mitigation: rollback the model version to previous pinned tag in serving-config, run a smoke generation locally (see local-smoke block below).

Escalation path (fast):
- On-call SRE -> if < 30m impact and rolling mitigation available, handle directly.
- If client-visible outage or > 30m no improvement -> page senior SRE (Nora Patel).
- If infra-level (OOMs, node flaps) -> page infra-oncall and add tag: #infra-urgent in Slack.
- Exec/CS notification: Only after internal triage and customer-impact confirmation (use template in Confluence link).

Local smoke checks (commands I run):
- curl -s "https://api.redwood.local/v1/health" | jq .
- prometheus query (grafana ad-hoc): sum(rate(tramline_request_errors[5m]))
- simple generation: python -c "from rlclient import Client; c=Client(); print(c.generate('hello world'))"  # local docker context required

Temporary routing snippet (copy-paste caution):
- api call: POST /api/route/policy
  payload: {
    "name": "tramline-temp-override-<date>",
    "predicate": {"region": "us-west-2", "tier": "standard"},
    "action": {"prefer_pool": "ded-flatpool"},
    "ttl_minutes": 30
  }
- Always include ttl_minutes and a changelog comment. Add a rollback note.

Notes to self / TODOs (for next shift owner):
- Add a snippet to the official runbook for the TTL patch (SRE-3421).
- Confirm whether ded-flatpool autoscaler saw spiky CPU or steady increased queue length before scale. (Evan promised to add metrics hook).
- Follow up on ENGINF-128: planned hotfix for tokenizer mount ordering. If PR merged, monitor rollout for 6 hours.

Unresolved questions I had while debugging last night:
- Why did clients from eu-central consistently get routed to us-west? (look at route logs, maybe geo-mapping mismatch)
- Is there a new service emitting extra short sequences that blow up batching heuristics? (check raw request-length histogram)

Rough timeline from last incident (notes):
- 02:03 - first errors reported (increased 5xx on tramline-core)
- 02:07 - TTL applied to KV cache for pool tramline-a
- 02:15 - ded-flatpool scaled up +1
- 02:28 - succeeded in eliminating most 5xx, tail latency drifting back to normal
- 03:10 - postmortem draft created (SRE-3421)

If you need to roll back a model quickly (cheat-sheet):
1) fetch serving-config: curl -s http://cfg-api.internal/serving/tramline | jq .currentModel
2) edit patch to set modelTag = <previous-tag>
3) kubectl apply -f tmp-model-patch.yaml && watch -n5 kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=tramline
4) sanity check: run local smoke generation and look for tokenization errors.

Final quick reminders:
- Leave a note in Confluence when you make a temporary change (title: Tramline temporary change YYYY-MM-DD).
- Tag incidents with SRE-3421 if KV-cache TTL was used.
- If you leave shift with open mitigations, put a short summary in the PD incident description and ping the oncoming shift in Slack.

Freeform scratchspace (random bits I scribbled):
- Could add a short Grafana panel: "kv-ttl-applied_events" to surface TTL patches.
- Maybe a webhook that auto-attaches route policy changes to the incident in PagerDuty.
- Quick checklist for customer comms: 1) impact, 2) mitigation, 3) ETA for fix, 4) contact (SRE secondary)

— Marcel
(leave note if you used any of the TTL/route workarounds)
